introduction: Today, fifty days after Easter, we celebrate Pentecost. The Holy Spirit comes upon the disciples like a mighty wind and tongues of fire, and they speak of the mighty works of God in every language. Paul tells us that the Spirit makes us children of God who cry, Abba, Father. Jesus promises that the Spirit will teach us everything and remind us of all he said. With Pentecost, the Easter season ends. Come, Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts. Let us bring our prayers to the Father, in the power of the Spirit.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world: that the Holy Spirit may renew her and make her one in faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who were confirmed this year: that they may live by the gifts of the Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For a world divided by language, nation and fear: that the Spirit may bring understanding and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in fear: that the Spirit of adoption may free them and assure them that they are God's children. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that the Holy Spirit may teach us and remind us of all that Jesus said. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you sent your Holy Spirit on the Church at Pentecost. Pour out his gifts on us again, and make us faithful witnesses to your Son in all the world. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Abba, Father
reflection.body:
Pentecost was a Jewish feast fifty days after Passover, and pilgrims from many lands were in Jerusalem. The disciples "were all with one accord in one place" when suddenly "there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind." Tongues like fire rest on each of them, and "They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other languages." The crowd is amazed: "we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!"

The Spirit does not erase languages and cultures. He makes the one Gospel heard in all of them. From the beginning, the Church is meant for every people.

Paul tells us what the Spirit does in each of us. "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God." The Spirit frees us from fear: we "didn't receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but... the Spirit of adoption." And the Spirit teaches us to pray as Jesus prayed, calling God our Father. "The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God."

In the Gospel, Jesus links love and the Spirit: "If you love me, keep my commandments. I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever." And he promises: "the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you."

The Spirit we received at Baptism and Confirmation is not a memory but a living presence. Today the Easter season ends, but the Spirit's work continues. This week, begin each day with a short prayer: Come, Holy Spirit. Ask him to remind you of the words of Jesus when you need them most.
